# PGN binding {#sec-binding-pgns}

[Normative]{.status}

## Overview

PGNs are the parameter groups defined by NMEA 2000, each identified by a Parameter Group Number.
This binding covers PGNs on every transport that carries them:

NMEA 2000
: The CAN-based network connecting instruments, displays and machinery on board.

OneNet
: NMEA's standard for networks on board over IP.
  It is link-local, and carries PGNs with longer messages than NMEA 2000 where needed.

This binding is how framework information reaches current-generation displays, and how vessel data enters the framework for sharing and recording.

## Transport mechanics

### NMEA 2000

#### Getting current state

A participant can ask a device to transmit a PGN, as NMEA 2000 provides.

#### Receiving changes

PGNs arrive as devices transmit them, unsolicited or on request.
Each PGN is the change itself, not a link to the Thing that changed (@sec-change-notifications).

## Representation

PGNs that carry AIS messages are a transport of the AIS binding (@sec-binding-ais), not part of this representation.
Synthesizing such PGNs on board, rather than relaying what the vessel received, is discussed in @sec-ais-on-board.

### Identity and changes

On NMEA 2000 a device is known by two aliases (@sec-ais-identity), neither of them an identity:
its source address, which lasts only until addresses are next claimed, and the NAME with which it claims its address, which lasts longer but can change.
A device heard on the vessel's network is a Thing whose IRI the vessel assigns, as the authority for its own network; the IRI is opaque ([NCF-SEM-004](../overview/semantic-model.qmd#ncf-sem-004)) and does not encode the NAME.

A PGN that carries a reading is an update to the Thing that holds it, even when the value is unchanged, since it renews the value's validity (@sec-validity).
NMEA 2000 does not say how long a value holds, so the binding derives a value's validity from the interval at which the device transmits it.

::: {.callout-warning title="Open question"}
Which existing PGNs can carry framework concepts, and are new PGNs needed?
How does vessel data on the bus map to the vessel data vocabulary (@sec-vocab-vessel-data)?
:::

## Fidelity

A PGN carries a value, but not the IRI of the Thing it belongs to, its references, its version, a signature, usage terms, or provenance beyond the device's source address and NAME.
A Thing held from PGNs alone is therefore incomplete ([NCF-SEM-012](../overview/semantic-model.qmd#ncf-sem-012)).
PGNs also fix the units and resolution of what they carry, as NMEA 2000 defines them.

::: {.callout-warning title="Open question"}
What is the maximum message size on OneNet, and can a OneNet message carry what an NMEA 2000 message cannot, such as full identifiers?
:::

## Trust

NMEA 2000 messages are not authenticated: trust in them comes from physical access to the vessel's own network.
The vessel's gateway is the origin of the Things it makes from PGNs (@sec-origins), and signs them as the vessel (@sec-trust-security).
The PGNs themselves are not Things: each one's PGN, source address and NAME are recorded in the provenance of what the gateway makes from it (@sec-provenance).
See [provisional decision 0030](https://github.com/NMEA-Cloud/Framework/blob/main/decisions/0030-on-board-bindings.md).

::: {.callout-warning title="Open question"}
Can a OneNet message carry a persistent signature (@sec-trust-security)?
:::
